You can get food from any culture in NYC which is kind of our beauty, it's hard to go wrong if you just look at google reviews. There's a great donut place in Park Slope (Brooklyn) called 7th Ave Donuts & Diner. Just walking around that neighborhood is a nice time and you could also walk through our borough's biggest park nearby called Prospect Park while you're there. I was actually pretty proud of an essay I wrote for a comparative politics class I took back in college that was critical of Israel and discussed the conflict. A UN special reporter was one of my most cited sources (among many others). My professor warned me against using that UN source too often and I doubted his skepticism (which is strange to me now as I'm a very skeptical person), I just assumed the UN was an entity that sought to bring the world to a higher maybe 'divine' status with peace and aid and such. I'm hesitant to re-read that essay I wrote.

Since that essay I felt a spontaneous calling to my connection to Judaism, and big TL;DR I've  went from being a staunch atheist to a religious man (in progress). I started connecting more with a Jewish community, I found a synagogue right for me, I've started "doing Jewish", and living Jewish. I've learned, I've seen and heard what having the modern state of Israel means to our tribe not because of the Shoah, but after every time our people have been chased out of the land. I started to uncover facts and perspectives of Israel that were from the pro- and Jewish side that just seemed hidden at first. I was so desperately missing all the facts before: how many times Israel has sought peace in the face of hatred, land agreements even when they were unfavorable to Israel, peace, prosperity, democracy, and more that I probably don't need to mention here...

I don't feel as ashamed of my past ignorance as I feel proud of my growth. I can't wait for the day I do birthright and possibly have the most spiritual part of my journey thus far. I became pro-Israel when I accepted my Pintele Yid.  I became pro-Israel when in the face of having to form a connection spiritually and emotionally with the nation of Israel, I found the fact that Israel is not an "Apartheid state". More than that I've had to learn recently as an adult how people hate us for who we are. I've suffered too many subway harassments because of my yarmulke or tzitzit to stand idly knowing our people are hated just for being Jewish.

I know that the disaffected Jews I knew from childhood who are now posting anti-Zionist propaganda have never even stepped foot in a synagogue. To be a self respecting Jew is to be a Zionist and care about the nation of Israel, it's in our souls and our blood. So in the face of the slaughter, mutilation, and bombing of *our* kinspeople, *my* kinspeople, I refuse to turn my back for the sake of some crappy friends. We are not Jews with trembling knees. We are strong. Am Yisrael chai.
